subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support PowerShell expansion-bearing commands through one-shot explicit approval, or should OpenClaw document that these payloads are unsupported/direct-script-only?
rationale: Current main intentionally rejects `$...` expansion syntax in the approval analyzer, while the user-visible report expects literal command fidelity; choosing between a runtime approval-path fix and documentation is product/security boundary intent.

options.title: Land proven one-shot approval path
options.body: Require real Windows/Gateway proof on the open candidate PR, then use that fix as the canonical resolution for PowerShell `$...` commands.

options.title: Document unsupported payloads
options.body: Close or narrow the repair path and document script-file/direct invocation guidance for PowerShell expansion payloads instead of changing approval behavior.

options.title: Hold for deeper Windows exec design
options.body: Keep the issue open for a broader Windows command-fidelity design if neither the current PR nor documentation-only treatment is acceptable.

recommendation.title: Land proven one-shot approval path
recommendation.body: Require real Windows/Gateway proof on the open candidate PR, then use that fix as the canonical resolution for PowerShell `$...` commands.

likelyOwner.reason: Jesse authored the current Windows shell analyzer and command authorization planner that the candidate fix changes.
